parts.refutation: Two checks count against the record. (1) 'watchdog window (V1 and V2)' has passes false. The RP2350 watchdog LOAD takes 0 to 0xffffff us, about 16.8 s (Table 1249), but no timeout can be both above the 900 ms stall of V2 and at or below the 200 ms deadline of V1. This holds for any watchdog, so it is a V1-against-V2 conflict for the owner, not a defect of the part. V1 itself is refuted below as not found. (2) 'GPIO reset state' has agrees false. The record says the datasheet does not show the pins returning to their reset state after a watchdog reset. Section 9.7 states 'The ISO control bits are not reset by the PADS register block reset driven by the RESETS control registers: resetting the PADS register block returns non-isolated pads to their reset state'. Section 12.9.4 and Table 532 let the watchdog reset the RESETS block (PSM_WDSEL bit 4). The RESETS RESET register resets with PADS_BANK0 (bit 9) and IO_BANK0 (bit 6) at 0x1, held in reset. pico-sdk 2.3.0 watchdog_enable() sets PSM_WDSEL to every bit except ROSC and XOSC (hardware_watchdog/watchdog.c:53). A watchdog reset set up that way is therefore shown to return in-use (non-isolated) Bank 0 pins to their reset state. Only a watchdog-triggered switched-core or POWMAN-level reset is not shown. The RP2354B is a fixed input, so this goes to the owner and the part is not re-selected. Every other value read passes.

figures.evidence: The report says a watchdog reset is not shown to return the outputs to their reset state, and that pads stay latched. That misses section 9.7: 'The ISO control bits are not reset by the PADS register block reset driven by the RESETS control registers: resetting the PADS register block returns non-isolated pads to their reset state, but has no effect on isolated pads'. Section 9.3 (IMPORTANT) says gpio_set_function() clears ISO, so pins in use are non-isolated. Section 12.9.4 lets the watchdog trigger system resets through PSM_WDSEL and subsystem resets through RESETS_WDSEL. Table 532 PSM WDSEL bit 4 is RESETS. The RESETS RESET register resets with PADS_BANK0 (bit 9) and IO_BANK0 (bit 6) at 0x1, held in reset. pico-sdk 2.3.0 watchdog_enable() writes psm_hw->wdsel = PSM_WDSEL_BITS & ~(ROSC | XOSC), line 53. A watchdog reset set up that way is therefore shown to return in-use Bank 0 pins to their reset state: null function, output high-impedance, pulled low. What stays not shown is a watchdog-triggered switched-core or POWMAN-level reset, where isolation can latch. The finding is too broad as written.
